increments.title: A correction round of pure coverage gaps runs test-author and reviewer only
increments.goal: Let the reviewer classify each finding it returns as a coverage gap or a defect, and have the workflow run a round whose findings are all coverage gaps through test-author and reviewer alone, visibly and on the record.
criteria: The reviewer's structured return carries a per-finding classification field that says whether the finding is a coverage gap or a defect; it is a value the reviewer sets, not a phrase the workflow greps out of prose.
When every finding of a round is classified a coverage gap, that correction round runs the test-author and the reviewer only, and does not run the researcher or the implementer.
A round with at least one finding classified a defect runs the full four-agent chain exactly as it does today.
The workflow log()s that it is correcting coverage only when it takes the shortened path.
The reviewer's classification of each finding is recorded in backlog.json alongside the round it belongs to.
The reviewer's own brief states what makes a finding a coverage gap rather than a defect, so the classification is decided the same way twice.
The test suite passes.
increments.note: Accepted at review round 2 with no findings: the per-finding kind enum, the coverage-only routing in both workflows, the log line, the recorded classification and the reviewer's stated rule are all pinned by test-repo.sh drivers w17/w18/w19 and a backlog recorder case; bash test-repo.sh 71 cases exit 0 and ./test.sh all 6 suites exit 0.

increments.title: The UI test harness returns null for an id the rendered markup does not contain
increments.goal: Stop the argus-ui test harness conjuring an element for every id, so an assertion that reads a container the page never rendered fails the way a browser would, and prove the harness with a case in the suite.
criteria: installFakes in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs resolves an id the rendered markup does not contain to null rather than to a created-and-cached fake element.

Every existing case in the suite still passes, or is corrected to assert what the page actually renders; the report says which cases were corrected and why each was passing against markup the page never wrote.

A case in the suite proves the harness itself: it removes a container from the rendered markup and shows at least one assertion going red as a result, so the guard is part of the run rather than a manual mutation check.
npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test passes, with the case count reported.
increments.note: Accepted at review round 0 with no findings: installFakes now models the document as one mutable markup string seeded from public/index.html and resolves an id only while that markup carries it, three cases pin the null contract from different directions, and a dropIds guard case makes the panel assertion go red inside the run; npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 240 cases exit 0 against 234 at the merge base, so the six new cases are the whole delta. The file the issue named did not exist - commit 1c94c20 had already removed the conjuring harness - so the increment created the contract rather than repairing it, and criterion 2 was answered rather than edited: no existing case was passing against markup the page never wrote, because nothing executed app.js against a document at all.

increments.title: parse-agent-log reports a whole workflow run
increments.goal: Give bin/parse-agent-log a mode that takes a workflow run directory and reports the run as one thing, and point the retro skill at that mode instead of at a hand-run loop.
criteria: bin/parse-agent-log accepts a workflow run directory and reports the run as a single report rather than one transcript at a time.
That report carries per-agent-type totals, per-agent rows in the journal's order, a tool breakdown that shows failures, and which agents started without returning.
The existing single-transcript behaviour of the tool still works.
The retro skill's instructions tell the session to use the run-directory mode and no longer tell it to loop the tool over each transcript and re-join the results by hand.

No page left in the repository still describes the tool as transcript-at-a-time only or still asks a reader to re-join results by hand; the report names each page that documents the tool and says whether it needed correcting.

The report states where the tree differs from the issue's account of the tool, and each criterion is judged by the reporting behaviour existing rather than by a file the issue named having been edited.
The new mode has test coverage that goes red when the report drops a section or miscounts, and the test run is reported with its case count.
increments.note: Two changes. The account-for-the-tree criterion is new: ui-harness-null found the issue's central factual claim about the code already false - the file and function it named had been removed by an earlier commit - and the increment stayed deliverable only because a criterion asked for an account rather than an edit, so this increment, which leans just as hard on the issue's description of an existing tool, now asks for the same. The stale-page criterion's note was also misattributed to this increment's own review rounds; the rounds that taught it were coverage-only-round's, which spent themselves on pages describing the old chain after the behaviour changed.

return.summary: Add a run-directory mode to the log parser that folds a workflow run's journal and agent transcripts into one report, point the retro skill and the README at it, and pin the report and the doc wording with new cases in tools/log-parser and test-repo.sh.
return.plan:
GOAL
Give the log parser a second mode that takes a workflow run directory and prints one report for the whole run, leave the existing single-transcript mode exactly as it is, and point the retro skill and the README at the new mode.

WHAT THE TREE ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE (differs from the issue's account in three ways; the implementer's report must state these)
1. `bin/parse-agent-log` is a three-line `sh` shim that execs `tools/log-parser/bin/parse-agent-log.mjs` with the same arguments. All work happens in `tools/log-parser/`. The issue's claim that the tool has no notion of a workflow run is true: the CLI takes exactly one log file path.
2. A workflow run directory is `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<sessionId>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/` and holds, side by side: `journal.jsonl`, one `agent-<agentId>.jsonl` transcript per agent, and one `agent-<agentId>.meta.json` per agent. A journal line has exactly four fields — `type` (`started` or `result`), `key`, `agentId`, and on a result `result` (the agent's structured return). There are NO timestamps and NO agent type and NO step label in the journal. The agent type lives only in the sibling meta file, as `{"agentType":"uroboros:researcher","spawnDepth":1}`. The issue never mentions the meta files; they are the only source of agent type, and the report depends on them.
3. No page in the repository instructs anyone to loop the tool over each transcript and re-join by hand — that looping was what the session improvised, not what a page said. The pages that document the tool are `README.md` (the `tools/` table row for `log-parser`, and the `bin/parse-agent-log --latest auto` line in the code block under it) and `skills/retro/SKILL.md` (steps 1 and 2). `tools/log-parser/` has no README and no CLAUDE.md. So the fifth criterion is met by adding the run mode to those two pages, not by deleting a stale loop instruction from anywhere.
Also: `src/detector.mjs` already knows this layout — its comment on `findLatestSessionTranscript` names `subagents/`, `workflows/` and a run's `journal.jsonl` and deliberately keeps them out of `--latest`. The run mode is additive; do not change what `--latest` selects.

NEW MODULE: tools/log-parser/src/run-report.mjs
Exports three functions.

`async collectRunReport(runDir)` returns
```
{
  runId,          // path.basename(runDir)
  runDir,         // the path as given, resolved absolute
  agentsStarted,  // count of distinct agentIds with a `started` line
  agentsReturned, // of those, the ones that also have a `result` line
  startedWithoutReturning: [ { agentId, agentType } ],
  totals: {
    tokens: { inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreationTokens, totalTokens },
    counts: { stepCount, toolCallsTotal, toolCallsFailed, errorCount }
  },
  agentTypes: { "<agentType>": { agents, returned, stepCount, toolCallsTotal, toolCallsFailed, errorCount, tokens: {…five fields…} } },
  agents: [ { agentId, agentType, started, returned, transcript, stepCount, toolCallsTotal, toolCallsFailed, errorCount, tokens: {…five fields…} } ],
  toolBreakdown: { "<tool>": { total, success, failed } }
}
```
How it is built:
- Read `journal.jsonl` line by line, skipping blank and unparseable lines. Walk the lines in file order and create one row on the FIRST mention of an `agentId`, whether that mention is a `started` or a `result` line; set `started: true` on a `started` line and `returned: true` on a `result` line. Building rows from the union rather than from `started` lines alone is deliberate: a resumed run replays cached results, so a `result` whose `started` belongs to the journal of an earlier session must still get a row. A repeated `started` or `result` for one agentId updates the existing row and never adds a second one.
- `agents` is therefore in the journal's order, which is criterion 2's "joined to the journal's order".
- Agent type: read `agent-<agentId>.meta.json` beside the journal and take `agentType` verbatim, including the `uroboros:` prefix. A missing, unreadable or malformed meta file, or one without `agentType`, gives the literal string `unknown`. Do not strip or prettify the prefix — the report is lossless and the value is what the platform wrote.
- Metrics per agent: parse `agent-<agentId>.jsonl` with the existing `parseClaudeLog` and fold the turns with the existing `aggregateMetrics` from `src/metrics.mjs`; take `counts` and `tokens` from that result and add its `toolBreakdown` into the run-wide one. A missing transcript file is a row of zeros with `transcript: null` — never a throw.
- Double counting guard: `parseClaudeLog` follows an `invoke_subagent` tool result that names a `.jsonl` path and inlines that transcript's turns. In a run directory every agent's transcript is a sibling, so recursion would attribute one agent's tokens to another and count them twice. Call it per agent with a fresh visited set pre-seeded with every OTHER agent transcript path in the directory: `parseClaudeLog(ownPath, new Set(allTranscriptPaths.filter(p => p !== ownPath)), agentType)`. Recursion into a sibling then returns `[]` and each transcript is counted exactly once, in its own row.
- `agentTypes` is folded from the agent rows: `agents` counts the rows of that type, `returned` counts those with `returned: true`, the rest sums. Its key order is by `tokens.totalTokens` descending, ties broken by type name ascending.
- `toolBreakdown` key order is by `total` descending, ties broken by tool name ascending.
- `totals` sums every agent row.
- An empty or missing-of-lines journal yields `agents: []`, zero totals, `agentTypes: {}`, `toolBreakdown: {}`, `startedWithoutReturning: []` — and no throw.

`renderRunMarkdown(report)` returns a markdown string with exactly these six section markers, in this order and spelled exactly so (tests assert them literally):
```
# Workflow Run Report

**Run**: `<runId>`
**Run Directory**: <runDir>
**Agents**: <agentsStarted> started, <agentsReturned> returned, <n> without a return

## Run Totals
| Metric | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Total Tokens | … |
| Input Tokens | … |
| Output Tokens | … |
| Cache Read Tokens | … |
| Cache Creation Tokens | … |
| Tool Calls | <total> (<failed> failed) |
| Errors | … |
| Steps | … |

## Per-Agent-Type Totals
| Agent Type | Agents | Steps | Tool Calls (Failed) | Errors | Total Tokens |

## Agents
| # | Agent | Agent Type | Returned | Steps | Tool Calls (Failed) | Errors | Total Tokens |

## Tool Breakdown
| Tool | Calls | Success | Failed |

## Started Without Returning
```
Rules for the body: token numbers go through `Number#toLocaleString()`, the way `src/renderers.mjs` already formats them. The `#` column of the Agents table is a 1-based position in journal order; `Agent` is the agentId in backticks; `Returned` is `yes` or `no`. Under `## Started Without Returning`, emit one `- \`<agentId>\` (<agentType>)` bullet per straggler, and when there is none emit the single line `None — every agent that started returned.` (em dash). Every one of the six sections is emitted even when its table is empty, so a dropped section is a visible diff.

`renderRunJson(report)` returns `JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)`.

CLI: tools/log-parser/bin/parse-agent-log.mjs
- Declare a new option `'latest-run': { type: 'boolean', default: false }`.
- Resolution order: if `--latest-run` is given, take the run directory from the new `getLatestRunDir()` and error out with `Error: No workflow run directory found.` on exit 1 when there is none. Otherwise take the positional as today.
- If the resolved path is a directory, it is run mode: require `journal.jsonl` inside it, and when it is absent print `Error: Not a workflow run directory (no journal.jsonl): <path>` to stderr and exit 1. Otherwise `collectRunReport` it and render with `renderRunMarkdown`/`renderRunJson`.
- Run mode reuses the existing `--format markdown|json|all`, `--out` and `--metrics-out` handling unchanged; keep one code path for the output plumbing and switch only which pair of strings feeds it.
- A path that is a file keeps today's behaviour exactly: detect format, parse, `normalizeSession`, `renderMarkdown`/`renderJson`, same exit codes (1 for a missing path, 2 for an unknown format or a parse failure).
- Extend the `--help` text with the two new lines: the run-directory positional and `--latest-run`.

DISCOVERY: tools/log-parser/src/detector.mjs
Add `export function getLatestRunDir(homeDir = os.homedir())`: walk `<homeDir>/.claude/projects` recursively for files named `journal.jsonl`, pick the one with the newest mtime, and return its containing directory; return `null` when there is none, and never throw on an unreadable directory (the existing `findLatestJsonl` walk is the model — reuse its defensive try/catch shape). Leave `getLatestLogPath` and `detectLogFormat` untouched: a session transcript must still never resolve to a run directory, and a run directory must never win `--latest`.

DOC EDITS
`skills/retro/SKILL.md` — rewrite steps 1 and 2 only, and keep the rest of the page as it is:
- Step 1 tells the session to locate the run: run `bin/parse-agent-log --latest-run` for the run that just finished, or pass the run directory `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<sessionId>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/` explicitly. For a retro of a single session log rather than a workflow run, pass that file's path.
- Step 2 tells the session to run `bin/parse-agent-log <run-directory> --format all` and says what the report carries: run totals, per-agent-type totals, per-agent rows in the journal's order, a tool breakdown with failures, and the agents that started without returning.
- Step 3's existing sentence about what a run leaves behind stays. In step 3's closing paragraph, the demand for a Session Metrics Summary table and a Per-Agent Breakdown table now reads as taking those from the run report rather than from a hand-joined loop.
- CRITICAL WORDING CONSTRAINT: the page must NOT contain any of the phrases `each transcript`, `each subagent transcript`, `per transcript`, `transcript at a time`, `rejoin` or `re-join` — not even as a prohibition ("do not run it once per transcript"). A test-repo.sh case greps for exactly those phrases across `README.md` and `skills/*/SKILL.md` and fails on a hit whichever way it is meant. Say what to do, once, and nothing about what not to do.
`README.md` — two touches, same constraint:
- The `tools/` table row for `log-parser`: say it reads a Claude Code or Gemini/Antigravity session log, or a whole workflow run directory, into markdown and metrics, and that it is what the `retro` skill runs.
- The code block under that table: keep the `--latest auto` line and add `bin/parse-agent-log --latest-run` with a comment naming it as the last workflow run reported as one thing.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES
- A `--run <dir>` flag as the only entry: rejected. A directory positional is unambiguous — the existing positional is already a path, and `fs.statSync().isDirectory()` separates the two modes with no new vocabulary.
- Folding the run mode into `--latest` as a third provider value (`--latest run`): rejected. `--latest` selects a provider today; overloading it makes `claude|gemini|auto|run` a mixed enum. A separate boolean is cheaper to read and to test.
- Sharing one visited set across all agents of a run: rejected. It suppresses re-parsing but attributes a sibling's turns to whichever agent's transcript happened to mention it first. Pre-seeding a fresh set per agent gives each transcript exactly one owner.
- Normalising `uroboros:researcher` to `researcher`: rejected. The mapping is a guess about a prefix the platform owns, and the retro reads fine with the raw value.
- Rendering each agent's returned `result` payload from the journal into the report: rejected as scope. The criteria ask for totals, rows, tools and stragglers; the returns are already in `backlog.json`.
- Emitting the per-turn transcript body in run mode: rejected. Forty-odd transcripts inlined is the output nobody can read, and the single-transcript mode still gives it for one agent.

REPORT THE IMPLEMENTER OWES (criteria 5 and 6)
Name the pages that document the tool — `README.md` (table row plus code block) and `skills/retro/SKILL.md` — and say for each whether it needed correcting; state that `tools/log-parser/` carries no page of its own, so there is no third. State the three tree-versus-issue divergences listed at the top of this plan, in particular that no page ever instructed the per-transcript loop and that agent type comes from `agent-<id>.meta.json`, which the issue does not mention. Judge each criterion by the reporting behaviour existing — the mode runs and prints the four sections — not by any file the issue named having been edited.

return.testPlan:
TESTS ARE NEEDED. Two files get cases: a new `tools/log-parser/test/run-report.test.mjs` for the report and the CLI, and a new section in `test-repo.sh` for the two documentation criteria.

== FILE 1: tools/log-parser/test/run-report.test.mjs (new) ==
Framework and conventions, taken from `tools/log-parser/test/claude-code.test.mjs`, which is the file to imitate:
- `import test from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert';` plus `path`, `os`, `fs`, `fileURLToPath` and `execFileSync`/`spawnSync` from `node:child_process`.
- One top-level `test('workflow run reports', async (t) => { … })` holding `await t.test('<case name>', …)` per case. Case names are lower-case sentences that state the fact, e.g. `collectRunReport: per-agent rows follow the journal's order`.
- `t.before` creates a scratch directory with `fs.realpathSync(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'log-parser-run-')))` and builds the fixture run directories into it; `t.after` removes it with `fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })`. `realpathSync` matters on this platform — /tmp is a symlink target and path comparisons fail without it.
- Fixtures are written by the test, not committed: a local `writeLines(file, lines)` helper that maps objects through `JSON.stringify` and joins with `\n`, exactly as `claude-code.test.mjs` does.
- `const binPath = path.join(__dirname, '..', 'bin', 'parse-agent-log.mjs');` and CLI cases run `execFileSync(process.execPath, [binPath, …], { encoding: 'utf8' })`; a case expecting a non-zero exit uses `spawnSync` so it can read `status` and `stderr`.
- Nothing is mocked. Real files in a scratch directory, the real CLI in a child process.

THE FIXTURE (build it once in `t.before` as `runDir`, and build the variants each case needs into their own directories under the same scratch):
`runDir/journal.jsonl`, in this line order:
1. `{"type":"started","key":"k-a","agentId":"aaa1"}`
2. `{"type":"result","key":"k-a","agentId":"aaa1","result":{"summary":"a"}}`
3. `{"type":"started","key":"k-b","agentId":"bbb2"}`
4. `{"type":"result","key":"k-b","agentId":"bbb2","result":{"summary":"b"}}`
5. `{"type":"started","key":"k-c","agentId":"ccc3"}`
6. `{"type":"started","key":"k-d","agentId":"ddd4"}`
7. `{"type":"result","key":"k-d","agentId":"ddd4","result":{"summary":"d"}}`
Meta files: `agent-aaa1.meta.json` and `agent-bbb2.meta.json` both `{"agentType":"uroboros:researcher","spawnDepth":1}`; `agent-ccc3.meta.json` `{"agentType":"uroboros:reviewer","spawnDepth":1}`; ddd4 gets NO meta file on purpose.
Transcripts, nested Claude Code shape (`{"type":"assistant","message":{"id":…,"role":"assistant","usage":{…},"content":[…]}}`, tool results in a following `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":…}]}}` line), one user prompt line each so each transcript is one step:
- `agent-aaa1.jsonl`: usage `input 10, output 20, cache_read 30, cache_creation 40`; two tool_use blocks, `Bash` (result without is_error) and `Read` (result with `"is_error":true`).
- `agent-bbb2.jsonl`: usage `1/2/3/4`; one `Bash` tool_use, successful result.
- `agent-ccc3.jsonl`: usage `100/200/300/400`; one `Grep` tool_use, successful result.
- `agent-ddd4.jsonl`: usage `5/5/5/5`; no tool calls.
Derived expectations for the base fixture: input 116, output 227, cacheRead 338, cacheCreation 449, total 1130; stepCount 4; toolCallsTotal 4; toolCallsFailed 1; errorCount 0; agentsStarted 4; agentsReturned 3.

CASES (criterion each proves in brackets):
1. `collectRunReport: the run totals sum every agent's transcript` [criterion 1: the directory is reported as one thing]. Input: `runDir`. Assert `report.totals.tokens` deep-equals `{inputTokens:116, outputTokens:227, cacheReadTokens:338, cacheCreationTokens:449, totalTokens:1130}` and `report.totals.counts` deep-equals `{stepCount:4, toolCallsTotal:4, toolCallsFailed:1, errorCount:0}`, and `report.runId === path.basename(runDir)`. Goes red on any miscount.
2. `collectRunReport: two agents of one type fold into one per-agent-type row, and a missing meta file is unknown` [criterion 2, per-agent-type totals]. Assert `Object.keys(report.agentTypes)` deep-equals `['uroboros:reviewer','uroboros:researcher','unknown']` (totalTokens descending: 1000, 110, 20) and `report.agentTypes['uroboros:researcher']` deep-equals `{agents:2, returned:2, stepCount:2, toolCallsTotal:3, toolCallsFailed:1, errorCount:0, tokens:{inputTokens:11, outputTokens:22, cacheReadTokens:33, cacheCreationTokens:44, totalTokens:110}}`.
3. `collectRunReport: per-agent rows follow the journal's order` [criterion 2, per-agent rows]. Assert `report.agents.map(a => a.agentId)` deep-equals `['aaa1','bbb2','ccc3','ddd4']`, that `report.agents[0]` carries `agentType 'uroboros:researcher'`, `stepCount 1`, `toolCallsTotal 2`, `toolCallsFailed 1`, `tokens.totalTokens 100`, and that `report.agents[3].agentType === 'unknown'`. Edge in the same case: a journal whose lines are shuffled to `started c, started a, result a, result c` yields `['ccc3','aaa1']` — order comes from the journal, not from the directory listing or the agentId sort.
4. `collectRunReport: an agent that started without a result is named` [criterion 2, agents that started without returning]. Assert `report.startedWithoutReturning` deep-equals `[{agentId:'ccc3', agentType:'uroboros:reviewer'}]`, `report.agentsStarted === 4`, `report.agentsReturned === 3`, `report.agents.find(a => a.agentId === 'ccc3').returned === false` and every other row's `returned === true`.
5. `collectRunReport: the tool breakdown shows the failures` [criterion 2, tool breakdown]. Assert `report.toolBreakdown` deep-equals `{Bash:{total:2,success:2,failed:0}, Grep:{total:1,success:1,failed:0}, Read:{total:1,success:0,failed:1}}` and `Object.keys(report.toolBreakdown)` deep-equals `['Bash','Grep','Read']` (total descending, name ascending).
6. `collectRunReport: an agent whose transcript is missing is a row of zeros, not a crash` [criterion 1, edge]. Variant directory identical to the base with `agent-bbb2.jsonl` absent. Assert the call resolves, `report.agents.length === 4`, the bbb2 row has `transcript === null`, `stepCount 0`, `toolCallsTotal 0`, `tokens.totalTokens 0`, and `report.totals.tokens.totalTokens === 1120` with `totals.counts.stepCount === 3` and `toolCallsTotal === 3`.
7. `collectRunReport: a transcript another agent's log names is still counted once` [criterion 2, guards the double-count decision]. Variant where `agent-aaa1.jsonl` carries an extra `invoke_subagent` tool_use whose tool_result content is the absolute path of `agent-bbb2.jsonl`. Assert `report.totals.tokens.totalTokens === 1130` (unchanged — bbb2's 10 tokens are counted in bbb2's row and nowhere else), the aaa1 row's `tokens.totalTokens === 100`, the bbb2 row's `=== 10`, and `report.totals.counts.toolCallsTotal === 5` with `report.toolBreakdown.invoke_subagent.total === 1`.
8. `collectRunReport: an empty journal is an empty report` [criterion 1, empty edge]. Variant directory with an empty `journal.jsonl` and no other file. Assert `agents` deep-equals `[]`, `agentTypes` deep-equals `{}`, `toolBreakdown` deep-equals `{}`, `startedWithoutReturning` deep-equals `[]`, `agentsStarted === 0`, `totals.tokens.totalTokens === 0`.
9. `renderRunMarkdown: every section of the report is on the page` [criterion 2, the go-red guard for a dropped section]. Render the base report and assert each of these six substrings is present: `'# Workflow Run Report'`, `'## Run Totals'`, `'## Per-Agent-Type Totals'`, `'## Agents'`, `'## Tool Breakdown'`, `'## Started Without Returning'`. Then render the EMPTY report of case 8 and assert the same six are still present — a section that only exists when it has rows is a dropped section.
10. `renderRunMarkdown: the numbers reach the page` [criterion 2, the go-red guard for a miscount]. On the base report assert: the exact row `` `| Total Tokens | ${(1130).toLocaleString()} |` `` (compute it through `toLocaleString` the way `claude-code.test.mjs` does, so the case is locale-independent); the row `` `| Tool Calls | 4 (1 failed) |` ``; a per-agent-type row containing `` `| uroboros:researcher | 2 | 2 |` `` through to `` ${(110).toLocaleString()} ``; the tool row `| Read | 1 | 0 | 1 |`; the straggler bullet matching ``/- `ccc3` \(uroboros:reviewer\)/``; and that `md.indexOf('aaa1') < md.indexOf('bbb2') < md.indexOf('ccc3') < md.indexOf('ddd4')` so the Agents table keeps the journal's order on the page.
11. `renderRunMarkdown: a run where everyone returned says so` [criterion 2, edge]. Variant journal with a `result` line for ccc3 too. Assert the markdown still carries `'## Started Without Returning'` and carries the exact line `None — every agent that started returned.`, and carries no `` `ccc3` (`` bullet.
12. `CLI: a run directory prints the run report` [criterion 1]. `execFileSync(process.execPath, [binPath, runDir, '--format', 'markdown'])` — the call throwing is the exit-0 assertion. Assert stdout contains `'# Workflow Run Report'` and the exact Total Tokens row from case 10.
13. `CLI: --format json prints the run report object` [criterion 1]. `execFileSync(… [binPath, runDir, '--format','json'])`, `JSON.parse` the stdout, assert `totals.tokens.totalTokens === 1130`, `agents.length === 4`, `startedWithoutReturning.length === 1`, `Object.keys(toolBreakdown).length === 3`.
14. `CLI: a directory with no journal exits 1 and says why` [criterion 1, error edge]. `spawnSync` the bin against the bare scratch directory; assert `status === 1` and that stderr contains `journal.jsonl`.
15. `CLI: a single transcript still reports one session` [criterion 3, the regression guard]. `execFileSync(… [binPath, path.join(__dirname,'fixtures','claude-code-session.jsonl'), '--format','json'])`, parse, and assert `metrics.tokens.totalTokens === 1110`, `metrics.counts.stepCount === 2`, `metrics.counts.toolCallsFailed === 1`, and that the parsed object has NO `agents` key — the session shape, not the run shape.
16. `getLatestRunDir: the newest run directory wins, and a session transcript is not one` [criterion 1, discovery]. Build a throwaway home with `.claude/projects/proj/sess/subagents/workflows/wf_old/journal.jsonl` (mtime T+10), `.claude/projects/proj/sess/subagents/workflows/wf_new/journal.jsonl` (mtime T+50) and `.claude/projects/proj/session.jsonl` (mtime T+90), setting mtimes with `fs.utimesSync` as `claude-code.test.mjs` does. Assert `getLatestRunDir(home)` is the `wf_new` directory, and `getLatestRunDir(<empty home>)` is `null`. Remove both homes in a `finally`.
17. `CLI: --latest-run reports the newest run` [criterion 1, discovery through the CLI]. Copy the base fixture run directory to `<fakeHome>/.claude/projects/proj/sess/subagents/workflows/wf_x/`, then `execFileSync(process.execPath, [binPath, '--latest-run', '--format', 'json'], { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, HOME: fakeHome } })`; parse and assert `totals.tokens.totalTokens === 1130`. `os.homedir()` reads `$HOME` on this platform, which is what makes the override work.

== FILE 2: test-repo.sh (edit) ==
Add one new section immediately before the closing `echo` / PASS-FAIL block at the end of the file, in the file's own style: a blank `echo`, then `echo "=== the retro reads a whole run, not one transcript at a time"`, a comment saying why the case exists, then the checks using the existing `ok`/`no` helpers (`no` prints the offending lines indented with `sed 's/^/       /'`). Two cases:
R1. `the retro skill points the session at the run-directory mode`: `grep -q -- '--latest-run' "$root/skills/retro/SKILL.md"` AND `grep -qi 'run directory' "$root/skills/retro/SKILL.md"`; `ok` when both hit, `no` otherwise. Proves criterion 4.
R2. `no page documenting the parser asks for a per-transcript loop`: collect `grep -inE 'each (subagent )?transcript|per transcript|transcript at a time|re-?join' "$root/README.md" "$root"/skills/*/SKILL.md` into a variable (with `|| true`), `ok` when empty, `no` listing the hits otherwise. Proves criterion 5. Note for whoever writes the page edits: this fails on the phrase however it is meant, a prohibition included — the pages must simply not contain those words.
Both cases are counted by the suite's own `passed` counter and reported in its closing `PASS: <n> cases` line.

== WHAT IS LEFT UNTESTED, AND WHY ==
- `--out` and `--metrics-out` in run mode: the two `fs.writeFileSync` lines are the same lines the single-transcript mode already uses, and the plan keeps one code path for them; a case would pin the plumbing, not the run report.
- Gemini logs in run mode: a workflow run directory is a Claude Code artefact and has no Gemini equivalent in the tree.
- The exact prose of the retro skill's synthesis steps 3 and 4: unchanged by this increment, and prose is judged by reading.
- `getLatestLogPath` behaviour: untouched, and `claude-code.test.mjs` already pins that a run directory never wins `--latest`.

== WHAT IS ALREADY RED ==
Nothing was run for this plan — no test, no suite, not as a baseline. From reading alone: `tools/log-parser/test/run-report.test.mjs` does not exist yet, so `npm --prefix tools/log-parser test` today runs only `parser.test.mjs` and `claude-code.test.mjs`, and the two new `test-repo.sh` cases do not exist. Whoever runs the checks first reports their exit codes and case counts.

increments.title: backlog.mjs record takes the step return on stdin
increments.goal: Let the recorder read a step return from stdin as well as from a file path, and instruct agents to use the stdin form, so no agent has to survive a heredoc to record a summary containing quotes or markup.
criteria: backlog.mjs record accepts the step return on stdin as well as from a file path, and a return containing quotes, HTML attributes and newlines records correctly through the stdin form.
The file-path form of backlog.mjs record keeps working unchanged.
The agent brief instructs agents to record their step return through the stdin form.
Every other page that tells an agent how to record a step return says the same thing as the brief; the report names each page checked and each corrected.
The change has test coverage that goes red when the stdin form breaks or when the file-path form regresses, and the test run is reported with its case count.

increments.title: An agent that needs a live collector has a documented way to start and stop one
increments.goal: Make starting and stopping a collector for ad-hoc inspection a documented, reachable thing rather than something an agent improvises with a pkill, and name it where agents will find it.
criteria: A documented way to start and stop a collector for ad-hoc inspection exists - a script or an existing test helper made reachable.
Starting and then stopping it leaves no process holding the port, and the report shows that checked.
The agent brief names that way, so an agent needing a live instance is told what to run instead of improvising a pkill.

The report states where the tree differs from the issue's account of it - a helper that is not there, or a way that already exists - and each criterion is judged by the start-and-stop way existing and being documented rather than by a file the issue named having been edited.
The change has test coverage that goes red when start or stop breaks, and the test run is reported with its case count.
increments.note: Added the same account-for-the-tree criterion as run-report: this increment's criteria lean on test helpers the issue says already know how to start and stop a collector, and ui-harness-null showed the issue's account of existing code can be a squash commit out of date.

increments.title: test.sh catches a commit-signing misconfiguration before an agent commits
increments.goal: Make ./test.sh verify that commit signing actually works in the environment it runs in, so a signing failure surfaces before an agent's first commit rather than after its work is done.
criteria: ./test.sh verifies that commit signing works in the environment it runs in - a signed commit in a throwaway repository, or the equivalent check the setup allows.
The check fails loudly and says what is misconfigured when signing does not work, and leaves nothing behind in the repository under test.
The check does not make ./test.sh fail in an environment where signing is legitimately not configured for the run, and the report states which behaviour was chosen and why.
./test.sh is green, and the report names the command, what it covered and its exit code.

increments.title: The loop skill pages tell the session how to tell a dead run from a live one
increments.goal: Correct the loop skill pages so the invoking session establishes liveness from the task's own status and knows that a user turn kills a running workflow.
criteria: The loop skill pages tell the invoking session to establish whether the run is alive from the task's own status, and say plainly that transcript file timestamps do not establish it.
The pages say that an ordinary user turn kills a running workflow, and that the killed agent restarts from zero rather than resuming mid-flight, so an interruption costs a whole agent.
The pages tell a session that takes a message mid-run to check liveness and resume rather than to report progress from stale files.
The pages do not describe the periodic self check-in or the resumeFromRunId re-entry, which another issue owns.
No loop skill page is left saying something the coverage-only correction round made false, such as an enumeration of the agents a correction round runs; the report names each page checked.
increments.note: Added the last criterion: the coverage-only round changed which agents a correction round runs, and this increment is the run's last pass over the loop pages, so it is where a page left stale by that change gets caught.

return.summary: Closed ui-harness-null as done on the reviewer's acceptance (no findings; npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test, 240 cases, exit 0, against 234 at the merge base). The cut still holds seven increments and five stay open in their existing order: run-report, agent-affordances, collector-fixture, signing-check, liveness-docs. Two changes, both taught by this increment. The increment's research found the issue's central factual claim about the code already false - installFakes and tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs had been removed by squash commit 1c94c20 - and the increment stayed deliverable only because a criterion asked for an account of what the tree actually holds rather than for an edit to a named file. So run-report and collector-fixture, the two remaining increments that lean just as hard on the issue's description of existing tooling (bin/parse-agent-log's current shape; test helpers the issue says already start and stop a collector), each gained one criterion: the report states where the tree differs from the issue's account, and each criterion is judged by the behaviour existing rather than by a named file having been edited. Second, run-report's note attributed the stale-page lesson to its own review rounds, which have not happened; the note now names coverage-only-round, whose rounds taught it. agent-affordances, signing-check and liveness-docs are untouched: their targets are verified to exist (the recorder's file-path form was used to write this cut) or already carry the accounting criterion they need. Nothing was split or merged - five increments against six remaining slots leaves room for a re-cut later if one of them turns out to be two, and splitting on speculation would spend a chain to learn what a researcher will report for free. One loose end this increment left is deliberately not an increment: the reviewer observed that the test-layout sentence in tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md still enumerates one test file per src/ module plus independence.test.mjs, which the new app.test.mjs does not fit; it is outside every criterion of this issue and not worth a chain.
